conclusion.bounded_claim: Across two decoder-based VLMs the measured image-text gap moves in opposite directions: on Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct it narrows under all three adaptation arms (DG* reduction 98.57+/-0.44% both-position, 96.74+/-0.29% text-only and 89.41+/-1.01% vision-only over thirteen seeds, with disjoint seed ranges), while on LLaVA-1.5-7B it widens under all three (DG* change +73.27+/-7.54% text-only, +121.48+/-16.33% vision-only and +95.66+/-7.91% both-position over three seeds). Both decoder experiments place the vision side in the same role from opposite directions, but they differ simultaneously in training objective (contrastive against caption generation), parameter scale (2B against 7B), pretraining family, dataset (Flickr30k against MS-COCO) and training-set size (320 against 1500 pairs), so the sign difference cannot be attributed to the objective alone; no archived run isolates any single one of these factors.
supported_by_data: the direction of the change on each model separately, at the stated n
the ordering of the three arms within each model
the invariance of each model's sign to the text-side convention of the measurement
the absence of seed-level sign flips in the arm means on both models
NOT_supported_by_data: that the training objective causes the opposite sign
that parameter scale causes the opposite sign
that the dataset causes the opposite sign
any comparison of effect magnitudes between the two tables
the claim that LLaVA widens the gap on every individual run under the instruction-prompt construction (8 of 9 runs widen there)

definitive_control_design.minimal_design: Hold model, data, budget, seed set and adaptation-site specification fixed and vary only the loss. Use one LLaVA-1.5-7B checkpoint with the toolchain already archived in tools/_p820_llava_sites.py so the preprocessing, target modules and measurement are byte-identical to the existing run, and define two arms: (a) caption-generation cross-entropy, (b) the symmetric InfoNCE contrastive loss ported from tools/_p1150_qwen_clean_sweep.py line 253 (cross_entropy over the pooled image-text similarity matrix and its transpose). Both arms train on the same 1500 MS-COCO pairs, three epochs, batch 2, rank 8, learning rate 1e-4, bfloat16, and are evaluated with tools/_p1145_clean_gap_measure.py so the DG* definition is the one Table G already uses. Analysis is a 2x3 design (objective x arm) on the same seeds, with the frozen baseline measured once per objective, since the loss does not affect the untrained model.
definitive_control_design.decision_rule: If the contrastive arm narrows DG* and the generation arm widens it in the same model, objective is sufficient to explain the sign and scale is excluded. If both arms move the same way, objective is excluded and scale, family or dataset must carry it, and the next control is the same objective at 2B against 7B within one family.
definitive_control_design.cost_estimate_source: rate measured on the archived LLaVA run: 0.95 s/step at 2250 steps per run (docs/llava_canonical_2026-10-17.md), so six new training runs plus evaluation are roughly six times the existing three-seed sweep; the two objectives differ in loss only, so no change to the data pipeline is required
what_remains_uncontrolled_even_then: the contrastive and generation objectives may need different learning rates to be compared fairly, and the archived runs use one rate for both
a single model pair still cannot separate family from scale
320-pair and 1500-pair budgets remain unequal unless the Qwen side is re-run
